basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Accessories to Mechanical Ventilation Systems on Board Ships — Part 3: Control Dampers
basic_identification.sector_category: Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding / Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging (finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee and approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council of the Indian Standards Institution)

scope.summary: This standard (Part 3) specifies the material specifications, constructional details, and dimensional requirements for manually or mechanically operated control dampers used in shipboard mechanical ventilation systems to regulate, balance, or completely shut off airflow within ventilation ducting.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Construction & Finish Code (Marine Outfitting / Ventilation)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Certification Scheme (ISI Mark). Manufacturers of shipboard control dampers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to print the Standard Mark (ISI Certification Mark) on packaging or damper bodies. However, compliance with IS 5858 (Part 3) is universally mandated by national shipyards (such as MDL and GRSE), the Indian Navy, and maritime classification societies (like IRS or Lloyd's Register) during technical design reviews of marine ventilation systems.

requirements.detail: Certified dampers conforming to this standard may be legibly and permanently marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify manufacturing quality.

The damper casing must be fabricated from mild steel plate (conforming to IS 2062) with robust welded or flanged ends. The minimum plate thickness is scaled by damper size (typically 2.0 mm to 4.0 mm) to withstand operational pressure drops.

Damper blades can be single-leaf (for small sizes) or multi-blade (for larger sizes). Blades must be manufactured from carbon steel or corrosion-resistant stainless steel sheet, designed with ribbed or V-grooved contours to prevent deflection under high air velocity.
Blade spindles or axle pins must be manufactured from wrought stainless steel or high-strength steel to ensure smooth rotation and prevent atmospheric corrosion or seizing in salty environments.
Axle pins must rotate in brass, bronze, or self-lubricating synthetic nylon bushings fitted securely into the casing walls to minimize rotational friction.

Manual operating mechanisms must feature a rigid hand lever, a locking screw or wing nut, and a quadrant plate permanently stamped with 'OPEN' and 'SHUT' (or intermediate angle graduations) to secure the blade at any desired airflow position.
When closed, multi-blade dampers must utilize parallel-blade or opposed-blade linkages with robust mechanical pivots. Sealing edges must overlap sufficiently to minimize air bypass and leakage.

All carbon steel casings and blades must be thoroughly de-rusted (sand-blasted or pickled), primed with red lead or zinc chromate, and finished with marine-grade paints to resist sea spray. Interior air-passage surfaces must remain smooth and free of paint runs.

Dampers must be tested at the manufacturer's workshop for free, smooth operation. The blades must swing completely from 100% open to 100% closed without binding, catching, or showing excessive play in the linkage bars.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 5858 (Part 3) : 1970 (Reaffirmed 2022) is the national Indian Standard specification governing control dampers used as accessories in mechanical ventilation systems on board ships. Developed by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee, it establishes standard material and construction criteria for manually or mechanically operated balancing dampers. It regulates the thickness of steel casings, blade stiffening profiles, and the metallurgy of stainless steel spindles and brass or nylon bushings to ensure smooth, wear-resistant rotation in marine conditions. It also mandates clear 'OPEN' and 'SHUT' quadrant indicators with lockable levers, allowing crew members to safely balance and isolate airflow inside shipboard duct networks.
